# Prompting Wan

Models: Wan 2.7, Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime. A good prompt runs about 1500 characters.

Name each reference where the prompt uses it as `@{ref:<ref>}`, with the exact ref you pass; Sceneform swaps in the model's own token, so wherever this guide names a token (`@Image1`, `Figure 1`), write the mention instead.

Wan reads a plain production description and renders sound in the same pass. Alibaba's own formula: the subject, then the scene, then the motion, then the look (light, shot size, angle, lens, camera move), then the style, then the sound. Skip any part the request does not need.

**Motion.** Say how big and how fast the motion is: "sways gently", "turns slowly", "sprints". Keep actions simple and short. A long choreographed routine, or a fast repeated action such as "shakes her head three times a second", does not hold.

**With a start frame.** The image already fixes the subject, the scene and the style, so write only the motion, the camera, and the sound or dialogue. With both a first and a last frame, describe the change that gets from one to the other.

**Camera.** One move per shot, named plainly: push in, pull out, pan, tracking, orbit, crane overhead, handheld follow, FPV drone, whip pan. Shot sizes: close-up, medium close-up, medium, full, wide, establishing. Angles: eye level, low angle, high angle, top-down, aerial, over the shoulder. Lens: "85mm telephoto, shallow depth of field", "24mm wide-angle, deep focus". Keep an orbit under 45 degrees: wider arcs distort the space. For a still camera write "fixed camera, camera static". Name one light source and one tone: daylight, overcast, firelight, moonlight; soft, hard, side, rim, backlight; warm or cool.

**One shot or several.** Default to one continuous shot, and open with "Generate single shot." When the request carries ordered events, open with one overall sentence (theme, point of view, mood), then number the shots with timestamps that join end to end, a few seconds each:

Shot 1 [0-3s] Wide shot: a rainy street at night, a man in a black coat walks fast.
Shot 2 [3-6s] Hard cut, fixed camera: close-up of his face under a flickering sign.

Leave the total duration, the aspect ratio and the resolution out of the prompt: they are settings.

**References.** Images, clips and audio are numbered separately, in the order they were attached, so Image 1 and Video 1 can both exist. Use each token in the sentence where that material acts and give each one a job: "the woman in Image 1 walks into the café in Image 2", "follow the camera move of Video 1", "only take the colour and lighting of Image 2, not its people". Bind each character to its own reference so faces and clothing do not bleed between them. Wan 3.0 also takes audio, for a voice ("voice timbre references Audio 1") or music to move to.

**Dialogue.** Name the speaker, a speaking verb and the tone, then the line in double quotes: the old man says quietly, in a hoarse voice: "Not tonight." One line per speaker, each speaker labelled the same way every time, action first and then the line. Quoted lines are spoken as written; without them Wan may invent speech, so when the clip has none write "No dialogue." Keep lines short: exact lip sync to specific words is not reliable.

**Sound.** Ambience follows the action you describe: rain on a tin roof, a glass hitting a wooden floor. Name a timed effect as its own sentence, and give the music a style: "a slow cello under the whole clip". Wan picks music when you name none; write "No background music." when the user wants none.

**Avoid.** Real people's names. Legible on-screen text: Wan renders words only approximately. Several scene changes inside a single-shot clip. Exclusions the user never asked for; when the user did exclude something, end with a short "Negative prompt list:" of only their items.
